scope: Source-backed updates to existing console-to-mobile project records. Fields use names from the projects table; unknown mobile compatibility and hardware details are retained as unknown.

fields.status: Android status dated 2026-10-09 says playable on device; boot, input and 15/15 lifecycle gates passed on a Poco X3 Pro (Android 14/API 34). The README also records a Xiaomi Mi 11 Android 14/API 34 check. Android is built locally from source; a public distributable APK path is documented, but the app build is debug-signed.
fields.summary: Static GBA recompilation with an Android ARM64 build, touch pad, save support and on-device acceptance tests. Requires the supported USA ROM; the launch BIOS is a bundled clean-room emibios, not a retail BIOS. Physical test gates cover boot, input and lifecycle rather than a full-campaign completion claim.

updates.evidence_note: The Android README records Android 14/API 34 devices, touch/input tests and a 15-assertion lifecycle gate; it also documents source APK generation and distinguishes private ROM-embedded tests from public ROM-import builds.

fields.status: Latest release v0.8.1 (2026-10-13) publishes an Android APK; Android requires ARM64, Vulkan and Android 9+. iPhone/iPad builds are now produced locally through PadMint from the user's disc, with iOS/iPadOS 16+ required. Android Original gameplay with a Razer Kishi was accepted on Pixel 9 Pro XL; the current iPad release candidate has accepted controller/menu checks, not broad device coverage.
fields.summary: Mario Kart Wii static recompilation with Android and Apple-mobile integration. Touch, motion steering and controllers are supported; Android ships a ready-to-install APK, while current iPhone/iPad builds use PadMint. Users provide their own game data; a raw ISO/WBFS import needs a Wii common key, while an extracted game-data folder does not.

fields.status: Adventure mode and Quick Race are reported playable on Windows, macOS and Android. Android has a release APK and requires Android 12+, 64-bit ARM and Vulkan; the project was developed on an AYN Thor. Users supply a USA SLUS-20398 disc image.
fields.summary: PS2 code is recompiled to native code on first launch from the user's disc; the Android build uses Vulkan and the Mac build uses Metal. The app imports the USA Road Trip Adventure image, builds game code for the device and supports touch/physical controller play; a specific physical-device acceptance result is not published.
